answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small deposit that burns like an ember if peers prove misbehavior, while reputation accumulates only through verified work at one vertex of the trust graph. A newcomer may wander across many tasks, but each new identity starts with zero history, so an attacker must pay the stake and redo months of attested work for every fake account, making a thousand-node forgery far costlier than the reward it could extract.
